shape_notes: Six-barrel, hydraulically driven, linkless-fed gun in the upper nose ahead of the cockpit. Barrel length 60 in (1.52 m). Whole system (gun, ammunition drum, feed/return chutes, hydraulic drive) is a single palletised unit bolted in with four bolts. Projectiles exit through the GUN BLAST DIFFUSER on the upper nose 'just forward of the cockpit windscreen' (single muzzle port on the top centreline of the nose). Exact fuselage station of the muzzle: unverified.
colour_notes: Internal; only the muzzle/blast-diffuser port is visible.
notes: Rounds: 578 max (AO 3&2 NAVEDTRA 12308 1990 review answers: 'the system holds a maximum of 578 rounds'; FAS M61 page: 'F/A-18 has a capacity of 578 rounds'; Wikipedia 578). NATOPS A1-F18AC-NFM-000 (2008) weight/CG table lists 400-round and 570-round loads. FAS F/A-18 page says 520 rounds - DISAGREES. Rate of fire selectable 4,000 or 6,000 spm (FAS); AO Table 8-1: 4,000-7,200 spm. Gun weight 283 lb (AO Table 8-1) vs 255 lb (USAF Weapons File 2003 M61A1) - sources disagree; length approx 72 in. F/A-18D(RC) replaces gun with ATARS (not A/B).

colour_notes: Mk 80 series: olive drab body, yellow stencilled nomenclature and yellow nose band(s) for HE fill; shipboard bombs must be THERMALLY PROTECTED: bumpy/textured ablative coating, the words 'THERMALLY PROTECTED' and TWO yellow nose bands (AO 3&2 1990, p.2-3). Inert full-scale practice bombs are painted blue. Fin colour typically matches body (unverified per fin type).
notes: designation-systems: externally identical to Mk 84, PBXN-109 fill, Navy version has protective coating. Introduced in the 1990s (exact date unverified) - no aircraft modification implied. Weight unverified (Mk 84 class).

designation: Mk 20 Rockeye II (Mk 7 dispenser, 247 Mk 118 bomblets)
span_notes: Fins: 17.2 in (0.437 m) closed in carriage; 34.5 in (0.876 m) open after release.
shape_notes: Cylindrical cargo section, rounded nose fairing with Mk 339 fuze and observation window (fuze cover in handling), tapered tail cone with 4 spring-actuated folding fins held by a release band; two internal linear shaped charges split the case.
colour_notes: Yellow band around forward end of the cargo section (explosive); Mk 7 Mod 6 has thermal coating and an additional yellow band; inert Mk 7 trainer has a single blue band. Body colour (OD) unverified.
per_station: 1 on BRU-32 or 2 on BRU-33 VER
notes: Weight 490 lb (AO 3&2). Mk 7-dispenser family dims from NWC TP 7033 (1989) for CBU-78/B (SUU-58/B = modified Mk 7 Mod 6): 92.0 in long without fuze cover (94.5 in with), 13.25 in dia, fin span 17.2 in closed / 34.5 in open, 14 in lugs. Desert Storm Hornet loads: twins on VERs at 2/3/7/8, singles on 2/3/7/8 and 5.

span_notes: As Mk 20 (same Mk 7 dispenser): 17.2 in closed / 34.5 in open.
shape_notes: Same external shape as Mk 20 Rockeye.
colour_notes: As Mk 20 (yellow forward band).
per_station: unverified (Desert Storm tables show generic 'Mk.7' dispensers on VERs at 2/8)
notes: 750 lb (AO 3&2 1990). Dims assumed equal to Mk 7 family (NWC TP 7033) - inferred.

designation: CBU-78/B Gator (SUU-58/B ex-Mk 7 Mod 6; 45 BLU-91 + 15 BLU-92 mines)
shape_notes: Mk 7-type dispenser shape; subsonic store.
colour_notes: NWC TP 7033 figure shows yellow colour bands; body colour unverified.
notes: Primary source NWC TP 7033 (Sept 1989). Wikipedia lists CBU-78 Gator in Hornet armament; stations not documented.

shape_notes: Cigar-shaped thin aluminium container, NO fins (tumbles after release), 14 in lug spacing, two filler holes 31 deg down from the top (Mod 4), igniters/fuzes in filler holes and nose/tail.
colour_notes: Unverified (AO colour code: light red = incendiary).
notes: AO 3&2 1990: Mk 77 Mod 4 ~75 gal fuel gel, ~500 lb filled. Wikipedia: Mods 4/5 approx 507 lb with 75 gal. Length/diameter unverified. Desert Storm Hornet loads show Mk 77 on the centreline.

designation: LAU-10D/A 5 in Zuni rocket pod (4 tubes)
shape_notes: Cylinder of 4 aluminium tubes in an aluminium skin; frangible nose fairing and two-piece tail fairing (base stays as a debris funnel).
colour_notes: LAU-10D/A has external thermal coating (shipboard version); colour unverified.
per_station: 1-2 on BRU-33 VER (dstorm: either VER position)
notes: Loaded weight ~500-550 lb (AO training manual via tpub snippet - not opened). Dimensions and empty weight UNVERIFIED. 14 or 30 in suspension. Desert Storm: VMFA(AW)-121 F/A-18D 'Fast FAC' carried LAU-10s on VERs at 2/8 (A/B use unverified). A DCS-forum claim says Hornet BRU-32 cannot take LAU pods directly - unverified.

shape_notes: Cylinder of 19 aluminium tubes; aluminium open-ended tail fairing; frangible nose fairing optional; 14 in suspension.
colour_notes: Thermally coated (Navy).
notes: Manufacturer sheet (Arnold Defense): 59.8 in, 16.0 in, 155 lb unloaded. F/A-18 carriage NOT documented in sources found.

shape_notes: Cylinder of 7 aluminium tubes; open aluminium tail fairing; 14 in suspension.
colour_notes: Navy D/A thermally coated; colour unverified.
notes: USAF WF 2003 (generic LAU-68): 61.29 in, 9.80 in, 86 lb empty. Desert Storm Hornet load shows LAU-68D/A on VERs at 2/8.

shape_notes: Streamlined supersonic-capable case; some versions parachute-retarded; also usable as nuclear depth bomb.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: Wikipedia: ~3 m (9 ft 10 in), ~37.5 cm (14.75 in), basic weight ~227 kg (500 lb); retired June 1993. FAS F/A-18 page lists 'B-57 or B-61'.

shape_notes: Slender bomb with ogive nose and finned tail (parachute options).
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: WF 2003: Mods 3/4/10 751 lb, Mod 7 763 lb, 141.64 in, 13.3 in. Which B61 mods the Navy F/A-18 used is unverified (Navy-specific Mods 6/8 were cancelled - Wikipedia). Wikipedia lists F/A-18 as cleared.

shape_notes: Large streamlined bomb; length 3.81-4.15 m depending on version.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: Wikipedia lists the F/A-18 among B43 carriers; retired 1991; 935-960 kg (2,060-2,120 lb). Not on the FAS F/A-18 list - weak evidence.

shape_notes: Solid cast teardrop body, centrally bored for a signal (smoke) cartridge; crimped tail tube with fins.
colour_notes: Light blue (practice).
carried_on: unverified (practice bomb adapters on MER/TER, or PMBR)
notes: Dims are the USAF BDU-33 equivalent (WF 2003: 25 lb, 22.9 in, 4 in) - Mk 76 dims not separately confirmed. Hornet rack/stations unverified.

shape_notes: Thin-case cylinder with box-type conical fins; simulates retarded delivery.
colour_notes: Light blue.
notes: WF 2003: 5 lb, 21 in, 3.88 in. Hornet carriage unverified.

shape_notes: Thin-case cylinder, retarded-weapon simulator.
colour_notes: Light blue.
notes: WF 2003: 10 lb, 21 in, 3.875 in. Navy/Hornet use not confirmed in sources found.

span_notes: n/a (tank has no fins - verify from photos)
shape_notes: Length/diameter UNVERIFIED (no public drawing found). Gravity/pressure refuel cap on top, precheck valve (NATOPS preflight).
colour_notes: Normally airframe grey (unverified).
notes: NATOPS Fig 4-4 (2008): tanks only on 3, 5, 7; configuration weights E454/429, F2596/2673 lb for a single centreline '315/330 gal' tank -> interpreted 330 gal: 429 lb empty (194.6 kg), 2,673 lb full (1,212 kg) (interpretation of the slash notation is mine). Carriage 1.6 IMN; carrier landing with >500 lb in the centreline tank prohibited. designation-systems calls FPU-8/A a '350 Gal.' tank - DISAGREES with 330 gal (NATOPS, Wikipedia).

shape_notes: Dimensions unverified. NATOPS mentions a 'cylindrical tank' (prohibited on centreline aboard carriers with non-flush deck catapults); whether that is the 315 gal tank is not stated in the text read.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: designation-systems: FPU-6/A 315 gal, F/A-18A/B/C/D. NATOPS Fig 4-4 interpretation: 454 lb empty, 2,596 lb full.

designation: AN/AAS-38 NITE Hawk targeting FLIR pod (AAS-38A/B with laser)
shape_notes: Cylindrical pod; forward section = rotating optics stabiliser (+30 to -150 deg look angles) with window; aft section = FLIR receiver.
colour_notes: Unverified (grey).
notes: Wikipedia (citing Forecast Intl): 182.88 cm (72 in) long, ~33 cm dia; AAS-38 154.36 kg (340 lb), AAS-38A 172.52 kg, AAS-38B 167.98 kg. Original AAS-38 = FLIR only (A/B era, limited numbers in Desert Storm on Navy and USMC Hornets); AAS-38A laser designator from 1993 and AAS-38B LST are tied to Night Attack C/D (FAS) - A+ use unverified.

designation: AN/ASQ-173 LDT/SCAM laser spot tracker / strike camera pod
shape_notes: Slim pod: PAVE PENNY-derived laser spot tracker in the nose, 35 mm strike camera in the tail. Dimensions unverified.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: FAS: Martin-Marietta derivative of PAVE PENNY, cannot designate. NATOPS preflight lists 'LDT/SCAM' on the right fuselage station. Dims/weight not found.

shape_notes: Wide-FOV nav FLIR pod. Dims unverified.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: C/D night-attack item (Lot 12+); permanent clearance Oct 1992 (dstorm). Not an A/B store - listed so it is NOT modelled on A/B.

shape_notes: Data-link pod (antenna pod). Dimensions unverified.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: Desert Storm Hornet Walleye load: AN/AWW-9A on centreline 5 (dstorm). NATOPS TAC menu lists 'AWW-9/13'.

shape_notes: Data-link pod for Walleye/SLAM/SLAM-ER (and JSOW-C). Dimensions unverified.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: Stations from the C/D SLAM-ER interim flight clearance (FAS): AWW-13 on 2/8 (config II) or 3/5/7 (config I/II). Introduction date vs A/B service and A/B-specific clearance unverified.

shape_notes: Cylindrical pod with rotating nose sensor head; station-4 version is a 'left-handed' pod with its own mounting pylon.
colour_notes: Unverified (grey).
notes: 2.20 m, 40.6 cm, 208 kg (Wikipedia). Station 4: 2005 contract for left-handed pods 'designed for pylon station four, the same location ... on F/A-18C/Ds' (Military & Aerospace Electronics). Station 5: Marines first used pods borrowed from AV-8Bs on station 5 via a quick-reaction mod (Defencetalk, via search summary). USMC use on A+ inferred, not quoted.

shape_notes: Training/threat-simulation jammer pod (ULQ-21 modules), many variants. Dimensions unverified.
colour_notes: FAS photo caption describes a blue ALQ-167 on an A-6 (colour on Hornet unverified).
notes: F/A-18 carriage not documented in sources found.

shape_notes: AIM-9-sized cylindrical pod carried on the wingtip LAU-7 in place of a missile. Exact dims unverified.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: FAS-quoted C/D SLAM-ER clearance lists 'ballasted ARDS pod' and 'ballasted EATS pod' on stations 1/9. Diameter assumed 5 in (AIM-9 form factor) - unverified.

shape_notes: Internal to the SUU-62/63 pylons; 14 in and 30 in suspension hooks; automatic sway braces; two-cartridge primary ejection, one-cartridge auxiliary (hooks-open) release.
colour_notes: n/a (inside pylon; sway braces visible).
notes: Carries single stores, BRU-33/A VERs and LAU-115/117/118 launchers. Emergency jettison releases everything on BRU-32s at 2,3,5,7,8 in pairs 2/8, 3/7, then 5 (NATOPS).

designation: BRU-33/A VER and BRU-33A/A CVER (twin rack)
shape_notes: Accessory rack hung on the BRU-32/A: two side-by-side ejector units with 14 in hooks and sway braces; on the BRU-33A/A (CVER) the ejector units are canted 5 deg outboard to clear large-diameter stores.
colour_notes: Unverified.
per_station: 1 rack per station, carrying 2 stores of up to 1,000 lb each
notes: Station list from AO 3&2 (1990) Fig 14-21. Dimensions/weight not found.

designation: MER/TER (A/A37B-6E MER, A/A37B-5E TER; BRU-41/42 improved; 'MER-7')
shape_notes: Strongback with 6 (MER) or 3 (TER) ejector units, 14 in hook pairs; practice-bomb adapters available.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: NATOPS (2008) section-takeoff rules mention 'VERS, MERS, TERS' and the CG table lists 'MER-7' on stations 2,3,5,7,8 - so some MER use is implied, but loads/stations are unverified. Not in the 1990 AO F/A-18 station chart. TALD carried on TERs (Wikipedia).

shape_notes: Twin-store MIL-STD-1760 rack. Dims unverified.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: designation-systems: used for AGM-154/JDAM/WCMD on F/A-18. WF 2003: 8x GBU-38 on F-18 via BRU-55. A+ use unverified.

shape_notes: Rail launcher housing with nitrogen receiver (3,200 psig bottle for seeker cooling), power supply, mechanism; forward/aft fairings.
colour_notes: Unverified.
per_station: 1 at 1/9 (always fitted); 2 side-mounted on LAU-115/A at 2/8
notes: NATOPS prohibits flight without the LAU-7A wingtip rails. Desert Storm Hornets used LAU-7/A-6 (dstorm). Dims/weight not found.

designation: LAU-115/A and LAU-115A/A wing missile launcher
shape_notes: AIM-7 rail launcher hung from the BRU-32 in the outboard pylon; side attachment points for one or two LAU-7 (AIM-9) or LAU-127 (AIM-120/AIM-9).
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: Stations 2/8 only (AO 1990 Fig 14-21). Length 82 in / weight 52 lb come from a tpub search fragment of NAVEDTRA 14313 Table 3-3 - LOW confidence, variant unclear.

designation: LAU-116/A and LAU-116A/A fuselage missile launcher
shape_notes: Ejection launcher mounted internally in fuselage cavities (left/right handed) so the missile rides semi-recessed; two CCU-45 impulse cartridges.
colour_notes: n/a
notes: LAU-116A/A also launches AIM-120 (A+). Latch assembly also listed at 4/6 (pod/adapter mounting).

shape_notes: Rail launcher for AIM-120 and AIM-9; on Hornet attached to the sides of the LAU-115.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: Dims not found (USAF LAU-128A/A for comparison: 103.14 in, 87 lb - WF 2003, different launcher). Wingtip use on A+ unverified.

shape_notes: Box-section rail with lug fittings, front/rear fairings and aft electronics; 14 or 30 in suspension.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: Stations from AO 1990 Fig 14-21. Dims are USAF LAU-117A(V)3/A (WF 2003: 94 in, 11x11 in, 125-145 lb) - Navy (V)2/A assumed similar.

shape_notes: Structurally modified Aero 5B-1 rail launcher with fore/aft fairings.
colour_notes: Unverified.
notes: Dims are USAF LAU-118(V)4/A (WF 2003); Navy (V)1/A is electrically different (FAS); external match assumed.

shape_notes: Centreline pylon housing a BRU-32/A. Dims unverified.
colour_notes: Airframe grey (unverified).
notes: Model-kit vendor listings distinguish SUU-62/A (early A/B) from SUU-62A/A (A+/C/D) - low-confidence source for that split.

shape_notes: Wing pylon housing a BRU-32/A. Dims unverified. Pylon variants differ by production block (check photos).
colour_notes: Airframe grey (unverified).
notes: Desert Storm USMC: SUU-63A on VMFA-314/333/451 (A models), SUU-63A/A on VMFA-212/232/235, SUU-63C/A on VMFA(AW)-121 (dstorm). Kit vendor: SUU-63/A for BuNo 161353-163175 (A/B).
